text: A few days after this chapter's models went live, the nightly dbt build job's test step fails. A unique test on fct_orders order_id — exactly the test Lesson 8 added — got 14 results, configured to fail if not zero.

A number alone isn't enough to act on. The first job isn't fixing anything — it's reproducing the problem on your own screen. Group fct_orders by order_id, filter for count greater than one, run it directly in Snowflake.

Now isolate the variable. Check whether this same test passed back in Lesson 8. It did. That's the single most useful fact here — something changed between then and now, most likely new rows landing through this model's incremental runs, not the model's own SQL.

A test that passed on smaller, earlier data and now fails on more of it, with no code change, points at which rows exist now that didn't before. Recall Lesson 6's own note: the payments join was flagged as worth watching. That's a lead, not an accusation yet.
Next lesson: finding the real cause — checking row counts before and after the payments join to confirm, or rule out, exactly what's happening.
